thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @eng-sre @eng-runtime — MercuryHealth (VPC, dedicated pool) reporting model regressions and high 95th/99th latency on prod routes. Error spike + user-reported hallucinations. Ticket: INC-78941

maya_oncall: acked. I'm on it. summary?

devon_support: Customer started seeing bad summaries at 09:14 UTC — multiple support tickets tied to the same session id prefix. They say some clinical notes are being omitted, possible prompt truncation.

lucas_runtime: telemetry: request errors up 28%, median latency +120ms, p99 latency jumping from 900ms -> 2.3s for tenant MercuryHealth on model redwood-3b-q4. KV-cache hit rate dropped ~40% during the spike.

maya_oncall: looks like targeted to that tenant's dedicated shard. Any deploys?

deploy-bot: deploy finished by lucas_runtime 09:07 UTC — rollout: redwood-3b-q4 @pool-dedicated-mercuryhealth v2026.03.09

lucas_runtime: rollback candidate checked, no full rollbacks yet. Hotfix idea: pin tenant to safevariant v2 (quantized, shorter context profile) or switch to fallback-model with higher determinism.

anika_pm: flagging customer impact: MercuryHealth is an enterprise customer with clinical workflows — SLA risk and compliance concern if hallucinations persist. CSM notified.

sara_csm: I'm on a join with the MercuryHealth engineering lead. They're seeing intermittent hallucinations among discharge summaries. They're asking for immediate mitigation and communication.

maya_oncall: initial mitigation plan: 1) Pin tenant to safe-variant model (safevariant-v2-small-q4) 2) Route to regional fallback pool if latency persists 3) Increase replica count for that pool for short window 4) Post-mortem with model team. Any objections?

lucas_runtime: agree. Steps I'm going to run: 
```
# both ops actions run from eng-runtime node
redwood tenant-pin --tenant=mercuryhealth --model=safevariant-v2-small-q4 --reason="prod regressions/hallucinations" --expires=2h
redwood pool-scale --pool=dedicated-mercuryhealth --replicas=6 --duration=30m
```
I'll start the pin now in canary mode (route 20% then 100%) to verify reductions in hallucination signals.

maya_oncall: please also disable dynamic long-context batching for that tenant while we investigate: reduces token reordering.

lucas_runtime: doing commands now. pasting policy change snippet: 
```json
{
  "tenant": "mercuryhealth",
  "pin": {
    "model": "safevariant-v2-small-q4",
    "mode": "canary",
    "canary_percent": 20,
    "expires_at": "2026-03-15T11:14:00Z"
  },
  "notes": "Emergency pin due to hallucination spike. Rollback after validation or auto-expire."
}
```

deploy-bot: Tenant pin applied (canary 20%). CID: pin-ccf2b. Change propagated to control plane.

devon_support: customer reports immediate slight improvement on canary session they tried. Still seeing some laggy requests but fewer hallucination reports so far.

maya_oncall: escalate to model team for deeper root cause. @lucas_runtime, leave canary for 15 minutes then shift to 100% if signals look good. Also prepare safemode override if canary fails.

lucas_runtime: monitoring histogram now. p95 trending down from 1.8s -> 1.1s on canary. error-rate dropping to ~12% so far. I'll move to 100% in 12m unless regressions.

anika_pm: CSM pls send customer note: "We've applied a temporary model pin and are monitoring behavior; we'll follow up with a timeline and post-mortem." Keep language careful about clinical data; coordinate with security/legal if needed.

sara_csm: sending update now.

incident-bot: Reminder: page includes on-call escalation rule — if error-rate not <10% in 30m escalate to SRE director.

lucas_runtime: moving to 100% now. running: `redwood tenant-pin --tenant=mercuryhealth --model=safevariant-v2-small-q4 --mode=force`

deploy-bot: Tenant pin updated to 100%. CID: pin-ccf2b -> active.

devon_support: customer reports samples look "much more consistent". They're requesting permanent pin until model-team verifies root cause and certifies the main model.

lucas_runtime: note: pin expires in 2h automatically. We'll coordinate with model team to provide a remediation window. Also logging a safemode route in case latency spikes: route to regional-hosted-llm in eu-central with reduced context length for critical endpoints.

anika_pm: open action items: 1) model team deep-dive (owner: lucas_runtime) 2) post-mortem + RCA (owner: anika_pm) 3) customer comms & SLA mitigation (owner: sara_csm) 4) telemetry alert rule refinement to detect semantic regressions (owner: eng-ml).

maya_oncall: handing off to lucas_runtime for ongoing mitigation. I'll un-assign from oncall after status check at +30m.

lucas_runtime: taking over. I'll update thread with findings and attach relevant evals. For now, mitigation stable.

sara_csm: MercuryHealth confirmed they can continue operations with pinned model; they requested a technical brief in 24 hours.

maya_oncall: closing immediate page — will re-open if thresholds re-breach. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC-78941 flagged as "mitigated" pending post-mortem. If auto-expire of pin occurs without action, system will revert to original model and auto-notify.

lucas_runtime: preliminary note: early signal suggests that recent kernel change in attention scorer interacted poorly with long-context checkpointing on dedicated pool; model team will reproduce in staging.

sara_csm: thanks team. I'll keep customer updated.

maya_oncall: final note for handoff: document exact pin command and CID in ticket, attach canary metrics and sample diffs.

lucas_runtime: done — CID logged, metrics posted to INC-78941 doc. Will follow up with root cause timeline.

sara_csm: thumbs up from MercuryHealth on current behavior. They want more frequent updates during the RCA.

maya_oncall: leaving channel. tagging next oncall per rota. :phone: \n
(End of thread)
